svg.text: Tip everything out and match each thing to a picture. Everything here is drawn at the same scale as every later picture.
The computer. Two black strips of sockets (P1, P2) along the
long edges, tiny numbers at the strip ends. Hold it by the edges.
The side with the microSD slot and the dog logo is the side you use.
A slab of holes. Red and blue lines mark the power rails on each long edge.
A mini board (17 columns, one rail pair) works too.
Must be a data cable. A charge-only
cable looks identical and is the most
Fingernail sized, purple or blue, four pins
(a few have six): VIN or VCC, GND, SCL, SDA
in tiny letters. The small metal can is the
sensor itself. If the pins are loose in the
bag instead of soldered on, stop: that is
A square board with a dark glass window and four pins on
one edge: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA. The order of VCC and GND
differs between makers. Read yours now and write it down.
Getting those two backwards is the one mistake in this
guide that kills a part instantly.
The one with the round coin cell holder. Six pins;
only SCL, SDA, VCC, GND are used. Leave it in the
bag on your first build. No battery until you have
read the battery note in HARDWARE.md.
Male to male: a pin at both ends.
Any four colours work if you use
Not in the bag and not needed: a monitor, keyboard or power supply for the board. Your laptop is all three, through the USB-C cable.
